structured_stats.description:
The '''Boomerang''' is a starter tower bought for {{Coins|300}}. It attacks enemies by throwing a boomerang at them.

The '''Boomerang''' will lock onto an enemy within its range and aim for 1 second before throwing out a boomerang. This boomerang will travel in an arc and pierces through multiple enemies until it either runs out of enemies to hit or reaches the maximum number of enemies it can hit, where it returns back to the '''Boomerang'''. Regardless of how many enemies the '''Boomerang''' hit visually, it will always only damage as many enemies as what its max hits is set to. Although setting the targeting is possible and visually, the '''Boomerang''' will target enemies based on it, once thrown it will instantly snap back and throw it at the first enemy. This boomerang takes time to travel to an enemy. It will not throw its boomerang again until it has returned to it, meaning its actual firerate is capped based on how long it takes for the boomerang to return.

At Level 3, it will gain a second boomerang, effectively doubling its damage. This will also not function the same as the first one, as it will target the last enemy the first boomerang will hit. For example, if there are six enemies in a line, the '''Boomerang''' will throw the first boomerang at the first enemy in the line and the second boomerang at the fifth enemy. They will begin returning to it once the first boomerang hits the fifth enemy in the line and the second boomerang hits the first enemy in the line.

The '''Boomerang''' is primarily an early to mid-game AOE tower which from Level 0 can be used to damage [[Flying]] enemies and from Level 3+ [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies. It has a placement limit of 12.

{{Attr|Bloated}} (Variable) }} ==Description== The '''Elite Lead''' is a tanky [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemy that appears in [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] modes. It has high health and average speed. It initially spawns with [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]], meaning only towers with lead detection can damage it, and with the [[Stun Immunity]], meaning stuns are less effective on it while knockback does not affect it. However, once it loses all of its [[Shield Health]], it will lose its covering and also the [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] and [[Stun Immunity]] attributes it has by default. To compensate however, it will increase its speed to 5 once all of its coverings are lost. ==Logbook Description== "''Taking the same concept as the Lead, the Elite Lead are Swifts who have fallen victim to the same process as the Odds. Though, more careful consideration was taken for their armor due to mobility reasons.''" ==Appearance== The '''Elite Lead''' is a humanoid entirely covered with grey metal armor. Upon losing all of its [[Shield Health]], it will lose its metal coverings, revealing that it is an entity with grey skin, purple substance on its hands and purple veins. In its torso, it has a giant hole with a purple crystal. ==Strategy== *The '''Elite Lead''' has the [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] attribute until its shield health is depleted. **Towers with lead detection like the [[Engineer]] and [[Accelerator]] are required for dealing with the '''Elite Lead'''. ==Gallery== {{Gallery|{{GalleryHeader|Trailers}} Hardcore Rework Trailer - Tower Defense Simulator|'''Elite Lead''' in the game trailer. {{GalleryHeader|Concept Art}} EliteLeadCA.png|'''Elite Lead''' on its concept art. {{GalleryHeader|Miscellaneous}} ModernEliteLeadIconIG.png|'''Elite Lead''' on its [[Index]] icon. }} ==Trivia== *The '''Elite Lead''' is unaffected by enemy appearance [[modifiers]], such as [[Talk Like a Pirate Day]]. ==Update History== *'''5 June 2026''' - [[v2.0.0]] **'''Elite Lead''' added, replacing the [[Lead Boss]]. {{Hardcore|[[Lead]]|Wave 14|Elite Lead|Wave 16|[[Mystery]]|Wave 17}} {{Voidcore|[[Lead]]|Wave 13|Elite Lead|Wave 15|[[Mystery]]|Wave 16}} {{ZombieNavBox}} [[Category:Early-Game]]

{{Knockback}}Knockback |sandbox = Yes |tag = {{AttrTag|Second|Fly.png|Flying}} }} ==Description== '''Flying''' is an enemy type that makes the enemy fly above the path, making them avoid being damaged by most things on the path. Towers need flying detection to target these enemies. ==Mechanics== '''Flying''' enemies fly above the path, which grants them multiple perks. The main immunity that it grants is requiring flying detection to target them, making it difficult for towers without said detection to damage a '''Flying''' enemy. '''Flying''' enemies have various other unique immunities that are applied, outside of flying detection: # They are completely immune to being damaged by unit collision damage, even if they would normally collide with each other. #*This includes the [[Gift Bomber]], which cannot collide with '''Flying''' enemies, despite visually passing through '''Flying''' enemies. #*Some units, like the [[Rifleman]] or [[Missile APC]], can detect flying enemies, even if they cannot collide with them. #They are able to fly over road hazards, namely the [[Trapper]]'s traps and the [[Harvester]]'s thorns (and by extension the [[Farm]]'s). #*The [[Commando]]'s missiles, can still affect them. #*The [[Barricade]] can collide with '''Flying''' enemies, but they deal unit collision damage. Therefore, '''Flying''' enemies are also immune to this. #They are immune to being knocked back by towers. This does not mean they are immune to other effects from attacks that knock back enemies. #*For example, the [[DJ Booth]] can still slow down '''Flying''' enemies, even if the purple track cannot knock them back. '''Flying''' enemies may be indirectly damaged by towers, even if they do not have flying detection. For example, the [[Brawler]]'s ''Reposition'' ability deals damage to '''Flying''' enemies, though due to their knockback immunity it does not knock them back. If an enemy is applied the '''Flying''' attribute through [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode, and they do not typically have the attribute, all of the said immunities apply to the enemy, even if they visually remain on the ground. {| class="sortable wikitable pad-5 align-center mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:0 auto; width: 50%;" ! colspan="3" |Flying Detection |- !Tower !Status !Level |- |[[Scout]] | class="no-table" |None |N/A |- |[[Sniper]] | class="yes-table" |Full |Level 0+ |- |[[Paintballer]] | class="no-table" |NoneFrom Level 0+, its splash damage can indirectly damage '''Flying''' enemies, but this tower cannot directly target '''Flying''' enemies. |N/A |- |[[Demoman]] | class="no-table" |None |N/A |- |[[Boomerang]] | class="yes-table" |Full |Level 0+ |- |[[Slime Trooper]] | class="yes-table" |Full |Level 4 |- |[[Soldier]] | class="yes-table" |Full |Level 4

Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2. It has no placement limit. ==Upgrades== {{PVPTabber |{{Upgrade|Level = Level 1|Upgrade Title = Expedition Gear|Cost = {{Money|300}}|Image = [[File:Freezer Upgrade 1.png|100px]]|Information = 0.55 > 0.35 Firerate [[File:Cooldown Icon.png|20px|Firerate]] 15% > 20% Max Slowdown [[File:Slowness.png|20px|Ma

{{Attr|Bloated}} (Variable) }} ==Description== The '''Lead''' is a [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemy that appears in [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] and [[Voidcore Mode|Voidcore]] modes. It has decent health and speed. It initially spawns with [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]], meaning only towers with lead detection can damage it, and with the [[Stun Immunity]], meaning stuns are less effective on it while knockback does not affect it. However, once it loses all of its [[Shield Health]], it will lose its covering and also the [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] and [[Stun Immunity]] attributes it has by default. ==Logbook Description== "''Molten material was poured on the bodies of Odds and molded by the blacksmiths. If they were lucky enough to survive, it would be nearly impossible for the Leads to take damage. In fact, this worked so well that Odds were beginning to run from the selection process, with many dragged back. If the Odds still had their individuality, it was most apparent during this part.''" ==Appearance== The '''Lead''' is a humanoid entirely covered in grey metal. Upon losing all of its [[Shield Health]], it will lose its metal coverings, revealing that it is an entity with grey skin and purple veins. In its torso, it has a giant hole. It has two walking animations it can choose from. ==Strategy== *Cheap towers that have lead detection like the [[Engineer]], [[Mortar]] or [[Rocketeer]] are recommended against the '''Lead''' due to its lead coverings, though as it loses its [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] after its shield health is depleted, other towers can also help in taking it out. *The [[Cowboy]] and [[Golden Cowboy]] do not have lead detection, but their shots at the '''Lead''' still count towards their income generation, allowing them to earn extra cash. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Concept Art}} LeadCA.png|'''Lead''' on its concept art. {{GalleryHeader|Miscellaneous}} ModernLeadIconIG.png|'''Lead''' on its [[Index]] icon. }} ==Trivia== *The '''Lead''' is unaffected by enemy appearance [[modifiers]], such as [[Talk Like a Pirate Day]]. ==Update History== *'''5 June 2026''' - [[v2.0.0]] **'''Lead''' added. {{Hardcore|[[Balloon]]|Wave 12|Lead|Wave 14|[[Elite Lead]]|Wave 16}} {{Voidcore|[[Balloon]]|Wave 11|Lead|Wave 13|[[Elite Lead]]|Wave 15}} {{ZombieNavBox}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:Lead}} [[Category:Early-Game]]
